title.narrative: Output 1.2. Increased institutional capacity of workers’ organizations

description.narrative: The four National Centers in Thailand namely Thai Trade Union Congress (TTUC), Labour Congress of Thailand (LCT), National Congress of Private Industrial Employees (NCPE) and State Enterprises Workers Relations Confederation (SERC), managed to put in place a ‘new’ output in Thailand’s DWCP 2023-27, output 3.2.2 in place to achieve stronger ILO and tripartite advocacy for the ratification of ILO conventions, particularly the Freedom of Association and Protection of the Right to Organise Convention, 1948 (C.87), the Right to Organise and Collective Bargaining Convention, 1949 (C.98) and the Tripartite Consultation (International Labour Standards) Convention, 1976 (C.144). The National Centers together with Global Unions Federations (GUFs) and emerging unions (such as riders’ unions – gig economy) drafted a joint demand on 19 August 2023 to rally the government to ratify C.87 and C.98. The joint-demand was submitted to the government in October 2023. The National Centers have undertaken to prioritize the need of migrant workers especially in providing enabling environment for decent work and kicked-off the initiative with Myanmar in collaboration with the Confederation of Trade Unions in Myanmar (CTUM). The National Centers and CTUM a series of online discussions with the ASEAN Trade Union Council (ATUC) which resulted in the agreement to renew existing MOUs to protect migrant workers. Through this dialogue, the National Centers advocated for the union membership portability in the ASEAN which was reflected at Thailand National Tripartite Preparatory Workshop on 19 September 2022. The ILO provided the National Centers with knowledge products, tools and materials in an effort to strengthen the National Centers’ policy advocacy initiatives so that it can effectively channel the needs of workers to the employers and the government and engage meaningfully in social dialogue. The ILO advised the National Centers on the significance and role of the unions to the DWCP as well as the UNSDCF processes, especially in securing a prioritized action for workers and in reflecting workers’ needs. The ILO organized bipartite social dialogue and supported the negotiations with employers’ organization in jointly developing policy recommendation to the government.
